# NOTES: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR (George Griffith, 1897; Gutenberg #20173)

Front matter: Arno Press reprint 1978 (Riverside UC copy). Frontispiece "Hail, Son of the Sun!" (p.78). Illustrator Alfred Pearse. Publisher F.V. White & Co., London, 1897. Author's other works listed: The Angel of the Revolution, Olga Romanoff, The Outlaws of the Air, Valdar the Oft-Born, Briton or Boer?

Epigraph: Prophecy from the ancient legend of Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, his sister-bride: a Son of the Sacred Race who, for honour, faith and love, takes the hand of a pure virgin of his own holy blood and passes with her through the Gate of Death shall cast out the Oppressor, raise the Rainbow Banner above the Golden Throne of the Incas, and rule the Children of the Sun "when the gloom ... shall have passed away in the dawn of a brighter age."

Contents: Prologue (I His Highness the Mummy p.1; II A Physiological Experiment p.16); Ch I Back Through the Shadows (32); II Brothers of the Blood (47); III In the Hall of Gold (66); IV The Sister Stars (86); V How Djama Did His Work (105); VI The Waking of Golden Star (124); VII In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui (145); VIII How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back (168); IX The Treachery of Djama (188); X On the Rodadero (209); XI How We Took the City of the Sun (230); XII Queen and Crown (250); XIII How Djama Paid His Debt (262); XIV The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire (271).

Illustrations: "Hail, Son of the Sun!" (frontis); "Am I only dreaming that the death-sleep is over?" (p.26); "The dagger-point dropped till it was within an inch of Golden Star's breast" (p.119); "They thrust him in with his arms still bound" (p.205); "It had smitten him to the heart" (p.228); "Now the moment for the giving of the Sign had come" (p.280).

---

## PROLOGUE I: HIS HIGHNESS THE MUMMY

- Setting: large study/museum, old house, Maida Vale, London.
- **Prof. Martin Lamson**: top South American antiquities authority; just back from a year in Peru and Bolivia. Called "the professor."
- **Dr Laurens Djama**: physiologist, ~32, slender, olive skin, straight black hair, blue-black eyes, Eastern origin. Saved Lamson from calentura in Panama five years earlier. Believed near occultism.
- Mummy: Inca prince, ~7 ft case, lying supine, hands crossed, face well preserved, dull brown hair, aquiline features, pale bronze skin. Lying flat (Peruvian mummies normally sitting, legs bound to chest, upright); abdomen not eviscerated (unlike embalmed practice).
- Djama's theory: suspended animation via unknown drug/hypnosis; cites Hindoo fakirs buried six weeks.
- Lamson's account: found in a round valley with a lake, four days' ride west of Cuzco, en route to Abancay across the Apurimac; mule lame; hidden behind mortarless Inca masonry under overhanging ledge. Arriero **Patricio** sent away for provisions. Mummy lay on vicuña skins in a dry rock chamber. He rebuilt the stones; back to Cuzco, case made, mules bought, railway from Sicuani to Arequipa, then Mollendo, steamer.
- Djama locks door; proposes "Mephistopheles" bargain: half of Lamson's remaining life for half of treasure found via mummy. Proposes resuscitation experiment. Lamson agrees. Djama promises the Aymara/"Aymaru dialect of the Quichua" is needed; Lamson is only white man who understands it.
- Lamson identifies the Inca as **Vilcaroya**, if the heroine is Golden Star.

## PROLOGUE II: A PHYSIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENT

- Djama's laboratory in Kilburn (Brondesbury Park house, garden lab). A week of silence; three letters and two telegrams unanswered.
- Thursday telegram/note: "Come round to the laboratory and make a new acquaintance who will yet be an old one."
- Mummy breathing, alive. Djama haggard; "two days and nights" of life-and-death struggle; he opened eyes before dawn; Djama tested pulse eight hours.
- Lamson faints behind a glass-doored cupboard; revived with ammonia.
- Inca whispers "Cori-Coyllur, Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" (= "Golden Star, my princess, my darling!").
- Djama's sister **Ruth** to nurse him, posing as a patient from the Oriental Home, Whitechapel.
- Djama injects colourless fluid; Inca wakes: "Has the morning dawned again for the Children of the Sun? Am I truly awake...?" Asks for Golden Star.
- Lamson, speaking Quichua, tells him of 1532 (Cajamarca, Atahuallpa captured, Huascar murdered, Raymi feast, Sacred Fleece unkindled). Inca: "The death-bridal." Told he has been dead ~365 years. Vows Golden Star lives: Anda-Huillac swore to lay her where they laid him, in the cave by the lake.

## CHAPTER I: BACK THROUGH THE SHADOWS (Vilcaroya narrates, first person)

- Vilcaroya, son of Huayna-Capac, descended from the Sun. Sank into death-trance with Golden Star in the bridal chamber of the Temple of the Sun. Golden Star was taken away; he was borne away.
- Named **Ruth** "Cusi-Coyllur" ("Joyful Star") after the maiden who loved Ollantay.
- **Francis Hartness**: captain of English warriors, ~30, tall, blue eyes, golden hair and beard. Met at Panama town square. Agreed to help take back the land; Vilcaroya plans to use lust for gold of conquerors against them.
- Ship south from Panama. Arequipa ("Place of Rest"); Misti volcano (12,000 ft), Charchani and Pichu-Pichu peaks. Dialogue with the professor on volcano's dormancy.
- Route: Sicuani (Vilcanota valley); Cacha plain; Piquillacta fortress; Plain of the Oracle; Cuzco seen. Vilcaroya swears vengeance: "life for life and blood for blood."

## CHAPTER II: BROTHERS OF THE BLOOD

- Hire house. Professor known in Cuzco, has Lima permit.
- San Sebastian village (two leagues south of Cuzco): descendants of Inca nobility. Vilcaroya disguised in old shirt, poncho, sandals, broad hat. Guide **Ullullo**.
- **Tupac Rayca** (Tupac-Rayca), chief of the village, great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru (torn by horses, wife tortured). Vilcaroya tests him in Quichua; Rayca does homage (hoe on shoulder). Orders twenty men of the Blood to meet "an hour before midnight" on the plain behind Sacsahuaman.
- Ruth defends him in plaza: "For shame, Laurens!" Djama had sneered at "Indian compatriots." Ruth: "they are Vilcaroya's people, and he is our friend."
- Hacienda for sale 3 leagues west of Cuzco, 20,000 soles (£2,000). Djama objects. Vilcaroya insists: "Let the house be bought. I will charge myself with the cost."
- Reveals Golden Star is his sister and wife; Ruth horrified, says she'll go to England tomorrow.
- Lamson and Hartness explain sister-marriage is unthinkable in modern world. Hartness, frank and kind: "...if you took Golden Star to sit beside you on the throne of the Incas as your wife and queen... a curse." Vilcaroya calls him friend and brother.
- Djama reports Ruth is sent to bed.

## CHAPTER III: IN THE HALL OF GOLD

- Vilcaroya changes clothes; hides dagger and revolver (Hartness taught him revolver). Suspects Djama is spying. Uses Ullullo to bait Djama with $10 bribe to meet at end of street El Triunfo at 11 pm.
- Walks north; bells chime half-hour before eleven. Route: rivulet Tullamayo, Rocca Inca, Yachahuasi, rivulet Rodadero, Colcompata, Tiupunco (Gate of Sand), Rodadero pampa. Song as signal.
- Captures Djama, blindfolds, gags; Tupac with twenty men.
- Sayacusca ("Tired Stone") rock with steps, cleft, deep pool. Copper chain releases water; pool drains; hidden stair.
- Fifty steps down, turn right; ten spans, eight spans; silver socket; stone door opens. Forty paces, turns, chamber with copper-lidded stone chests.
- Imperial robes of ill-fated **Huascar**, laid in by Anda-Huillac. Vilcaroya dresses: golden sandals, mantle emblazoned with Sun and Moon, scarlet Llautu, crimson Borla.
- Hall of Gold: gold plates, jewels, pyramid of gold bars, two giant golden Suns with diamond eyes, ruby lips, emerald pendants.
- Djama: "Vilcaroya, is it you...?" Tupac and tribe kneel: "Hail, Son of the Sun."
- Djama threatened: fragments sent through Land of Four Regions if he speaks.
- Ten men carry gold in ponchos. Vilcaroya breaks torch.
- Men pledge; gold sold through professor and Djama as product of Vilcaroya's "mines." Hacienda bought; Ruth as housewife.
- Fifteenth day departure to Golden Star's resting-place.

## CHAPTER IV: THE SISTER STARS

- Five-day journey: Saljantai, Umantai peaks; Lima Tambo ruins; Apurimac ("Great Speaker"); Rio de la Banca; ruined bridge.
- Third evening: rock with three seats; twin peaks; lake and cave under cliff; Tupac finds hidden door; three lines on pillar; iron rod; tunnel.
- Coffin-case brought (padded, pillow of down).
- Vilcaroya tells Ruth his feelings; decides to take Tupac's firstborn as heir if Golden Star doesn't wake. Ruth touches his arm; their hands touch.
- Hartness approaches; Ruth says "Captain Hartness." Vilcaroya feels rage.
- Next morning: removes wedge stone; Golden Star lies on skins. Ruth first to see; likenesses noted.

## CHAPTER V: HOW DJAMA DID HIS WORK

- Golden Star carried to hacienda, laid on table. Djama works alone, no interruptions, two days.
- Third night: Djama wakes Vilcaroya. Golden Star in limbo "neither dead nor alive." Djama demands she be his wife/promised. Says he loves her.
- Vilcaroya threatens to torture him (cave walling, chain to rock, burn). Djama: "I am as much the master of my own life..."
- Vilcaroya's conditions: Djama must win Golden Star's love; Djama must give his sister Ruth to Vilcaroya if Vilcaroya wins Ruth's love. Dagger held over Golden Star's breast.
- Djama yields: "My sister for your sister."
- Ghosts of Anda-Huillac; dagger falls; Lamson and Hartness enter with Ruth.

## CHAPTER VI: THE WAKING OF GOLDEN STAR

- Djama drags Ruth toward Vilcaroya; Hartness stops him.
- Vilcaroya declares his conditions; Ruth refuses being "given away." Vilcaroya yields.
- Ruth pleads with Djama to restore Golden Star without price. Djama relents.
- Djama and Vilcaroya shake hands.
- Golden Star awakens: Ruth kisses her and she awakens with eyes open. Vilcaroya speaks "Cori-Coyllur..."; she has no speech/memory—child-like eyes.
- Ruth becomes nurse; men dismissed.
- Hartness and Vilcaroya's night talk: Peru's civil war; Hartness pledges to be war-chief. Gives word.

## CHAPTER VII: IN THE THRONE-ROOM OF YUPANQUI

- Golden Star awakens as 17-year-old, like her age at death. Ruth nurses her.
- Djama asks Vilcaroya for reward; Vilcaroya offers the Hall of Gold gold in exchange for oaths; Djama wants Golden Star and proposes she go to England with Ruth for three years.
- Garden: Golden Star and Ruth; Golden Star recoils from Djama (her child-sight sees evil).
- Golden Star and Ruth see the throne-room; Ruth seated on Yupanqui's throne; Vilcaroya proposes to Joyful Star. "Come sit beside me."
- Tupac and six men bring Children of the Blood.

## CHAPTER VIII: HOW THE SOUL OF GOLDEN STAR CAME BACK

- Sixty heads of Ayllos families. Vilcaroya declares Golden Star his sister and Ruth his Coya.
- Golden Star awakens: "Have they awakened us, my lord?" She recognises Vilcaroya. Ruth: "Is she your wife?"
- Djama's treachery: Djama plots with Governor of Cuzco (Don Antonio Prada?). Hartness addresses assembly. Vilcaroya gives orders.

## CHAPTER IX: THE TREACHERY OF DJAMA

- Djama went to Governor Prada to betray Vilcaroya; Spaniard's son is Coronel Prada. Soldiers under Spanish officer enter Hall of Gold.
- Djama and officer confess; Vilcaroya builds gold prison-cells for both traitors.
- Djama: "It was your own fault... Why did you not give her to me?"
- Professor Lamson swears secrecy; Vilcaroya says Djama shall live as hostage.

## CHAPTER X: ON THE RODADERO

- Ruth pleads for Djama's life.
- Golden Star plays with Ruth; Evil Eyes name for Djama.
- Anahuac and Ainu bring news: Governor Antonio Prada, son Coronel Prada; Sub-Prefect; dynamite plans.
- Vilcaroya kills sentry with knife; Hartness disguised. Vilcaroya kills officer with knife.

## CHAPTER XI: HOW WE TOOK THE CITY OF THE SUN

- Trap at Sayacusca; water and soldiers. Governor Prada surrenders; Vilcaroya takes his sword.
- Hartness leads cavalry; Gatling and Maxim guns seized at Cuartel.
- Vilcaroya proclaims Cuzco; Sub-Prefect guns cleared.

## CHAPTER XII: QUEEN AND CROWN

- Ruth and Vilcaroya declare love. Djama in cell calls Ruth "sister."
- Golden Star to Hartness: "Why does the Son of the Great People do that?"
- Vilcaroya's coronation at dawn on cathedral terrace; Rainbow Banner; Hymn to the Sun.

## CHAPTER XIII: HOW DJAMA PAID HIS DEBT

- Djama brought before Vilcaroya; threatens; seizes rifle; shoots and kills **Ullullo** (old friend, behind throne). Djama dies by willed suffocation (heart stops).

## CHAPTER XIV: THE RE-KINDLING OF THE SACRED FIRE

- Vilcaroya's campaigns to Pacific; Hartness and Lamson write the book; Joyful Star helps.
- Return to Cuzco; Santo Domingo church (footnote F: Church of Santo Domingo on Temple of Sun site, not Cathedral).
- Eve of Feast of Raymi; Tupac-Rayca High Priest (Villac-Umu); Hartness named "Viracocha."
- Golden Star lights Sacred Fleece with sunbeam; Hymn to the Sun.
- Marriage-font: Vilcaroya and Joyful Star join hands across double gold cup (red wine and pure water).
- Hartness and Golden Star take place at the font.

## LIST OF CORRECTIONS (printer's errata)
- "Anahauc" → "Anahuac" (pp.206, 208)
- "ont" → "out" (p.298 "mete ont justice")
- "Ullulo" → "Ullullo" (p.288)
